checked.claim: VoetbalTV EUR 575,000 (2019), annulled by Rechtbank Midden-Nederland, upheld by Council of State 2022; KNLTB EUR 525,000 led to C-621/22 (4 October 2024)
checked.evidence: Netkwesties: VoetbalTV EUR 575,000 issued 2019, annulled by Rechtbank Midden-Nederland and the Raad van State in 2022; KNLTB EUR 525,000; C-621/22 of 4 October 2024 contradicted the AP's view. checked.evidence: Standard Awb six-week term (Art. 6:7); the fetched Awb page did not render the article text, so confirmed on knowledge of the statute.

checked.claim: Not confirmed; Art. 6:16 Awb no suspension
checked.evidence: No specific suspension rule for AP fines found; a WODC study on suspending administrative fines during objection and appeal suggests there is no general Awb rule.

checked.claim: Five years after the infringement (Art. 5:45 Awb)
checked.evidence: Art. 5:45(1) Awb: power to impose a fine lapses five years after the infringement; article page did not render, confirmed on knowledge and secondary mention (handhavingsrecht.nl).

checked.claim: Eight-week default (Art. 4:13 Awb) 'alongside the three-month progress update in Art. 78(2) GDPR'
checked.evidence: Art. 4:13(2) Awb eight weeks confirmed. Art. 78(2) GDPR does not create a progress update: it gives a judicial remedy where the authority does not handle the complaint or inform the complainant within three months (the duty to inform is in Art. 77(2)).
checked.replacement: No statutory time limit for complaining was found. The AP's decision on a complaint is a decision (besluit) under the Awb, so the general Awb rule applies: the statutory term, or else a reasonable term that defaults to eight weeks (Art. 4:13 Awb). Under Art. 78(2) GDPR the complainant can also go to court if the AP has not informed them of progress or outcome within three months.

checked.claim: Amsterdam Court of Appeal TikTok ruling on 8 October 2025
checked.evidence: DutchNews (published Wednesday 8 October 2025): 'the appeal court said on Tuesday', i.e. 7 October 2025; reversed the district court on collective non-material damages.
checked.replacement: Collective actions, including for damages, under the WAMCA (Art. 3:305a Dutch Civil Code, in force 1 January 2020). On 7 October 2025 the Amsterdam Court of Appeal held in the TikTok case that non-material privacy damages can be claimed collectively, reversing the district court. Other privacy class actions run against Meta (Data Privacy Stichting), Oracle/Salesforce and Google.

notes: Most serious: complaint.deadlines mischaracterised Art. 78(2) GDPR as a progress-update duty. TikTok ruling date off by one day. Note the Council of State upheld the VoetbalTV annulment on a reasoning defect, not by endorsing commercial interests as legitimate; the summary's wording is accurate but could be read otherwise.
